role: Independent expert, production-plan.md section 5 steps 2 and 3 (blind solve, key check). Coach only; never published.
method: Each item was loaded from tools/mock/data/full-mocks.js with the pipeline loader (the vm window context scripts/explainers/build.mjs uses) and shown as served: stem and the five choices in bank order (tools/mock/full.js escapes the stem as text and does not shuffle). The extractor withheld correct, why, traps, src, stop and nights; only the field names were seen.

The served page was then rendered in Chromium at http://127.0.0.1:4107/tools/mock/full.html (FULL_1, Natural Sciences questions 41 to 70): all 30 stems and choice sets match the loader text exactly, no item serves a stem drawing or structure choices, and the page raised no errors.

Answers, reasoning, concept, a family and a misconception for every other choice, and confidence were written to a draft and stamped (sha256 c2dadc2482aa0b24, 2026-10-30T08:55:53Z) before any key was read; the key comparison then ran by exact choice text.

Every number and every distractor route was recomputed in python (K_p, Ksp root, crossover T, gas laws, Dalton, half-life, pH and buffer logs, van t Hoff factor, Nernst and log K, formation-enthalpy sums, Hess, mole counts). RDKit 2026.09.1 checked the formula masses and atom counts behind the mole items and the valence-electron and lone-pair counts for XeF4 and ClF3; no item serves a SMILES, so there was no structure or stereo to check.
Families come from the closed list in scripts/explainers/families.js; missType follows the family. They are suggestions for the writer, who decides.
Bank why and trap notes were read only after the key check, to flag copy the writer should not lift (bankCopy) and to compare distractor routes (notes); nothing in the bank was edited.

process.note: The blind view never printed key, why or trap values. The draft hash and time are recorded above; the key check and the bank read came after.

summary.line: All 30 keys agree with the blind solve; no key dispute raised, so key-disputes.json is unchanged. Writer cautions: the GC_pd5 bank why reverses the phase-diagram regions, three bank notes use house-banned words, 7 items carry a distractor with no single-slip route, and 3 items are arithmetic heavy for a no-calculator section.

expert.answer: It rises, because removing CO2 lowers carbonic acid
expert.concept: Le Chatelier on the blood buffer: CO2 + H2O <=> H2CO3 <=> H+ + HCO3-. Removing CO2 pulls everything left, so H+ falls and pH rises (respiratory alkalosis).
reasoning: Write the chain: CO2 + H2O <=> H2CO3 <=> H+ + HCO3-.
Hyperventilating removes CO2, so the equilibrium shifts left: less H2CO3 and less H+.
Less H+ means a higher pH: respiratory alkalosis.

misconceptions.choice: It falls, because less bicarbonate is made
misconceptions.pull: Bicarbonate does drop a little as the chain shifts left, but the H+ drops too, so pH rises, not falls.

misconceptions.choice: It does not change, because blood is buffered
misconceptions.pull: Buffers resist change from added acid or base; here the buffer acid itself is being removed, so pH moves.

misconceptions.choice: It rises, because hyperventilating adds extra bicarbonate to the blood
misconceptions.pull: The direction is right, but the reason is not: removing CO2 lowers bicarbonate slightly; it does not add any.

misconceptions.choice: It falls, because CO2 is a base
misconceptions.pull: CO2 is an acid (it makes carbonic acid in water), so losing it makes the blood less acidic.

key.text: It rises, because removing CO2 lowers carbonic acid

expert.concept: Hydrogen bonding (H on F, O or N) outweighs the extra London forces of a heavier molecule.
reasoning: Name the strongest force in each: HF has H bonded to F, so it hydrogen bonds; HCl only has dipole-dipole and London forces.
H-bonds are much stronger than the extra dispersion HCl gains from its extra electrons, so HF boils higher (about 20 C vs -85 C).

misconceptions.pull: Metallic bonding belongs to metals; HF and HCl are molecular.
HCl has more electrons, so its London forces are the stronger ones.
HCl ionizes in water, but pure HCl is a molecular, polar covalent gas.
Density is not a cause of boiling point; intermolecular force strength is.
